Your coding agent writes more code than you can review. You should spend your review time on design decisions and risky changes, not boilerplate.
diffmap is an agent skill that lets your agent explain its changes to you visually. The agent writes a spec with interactive diagrams, and each part of a diagram links back to its source code.
Want a cloud-hosted viewer for sharing diffmaps with your team? Upvote Diffmap Cloud so I know there's interest.
You can try diffmap before you install it. In a repository that has changes, paste this prompt into your agent:
If you like the result, install the skill:
The skill keeps a spec in specs/ that stays true to what is planned and what is already in the tree. diffmap is open source and MIT licensed. Specs are served locally by default, but you can choose to share one as an unlisted gist and open it on diffmap.dev.
Your agent picks the best diagram for each idea, and each part of a diagram links to its code. diffmap.dev walks through each one on an example pull request.
A service diagram shows each service and its state. Each step shows one event and the state that the event changes, so you do not have to remember the state. Press Play to step through it. See Animated service diagrams for the syntax.
A Mermaid or service diagram can show a change in one picture: red parts exist only today, and green parts are new. In a service diagram diff, each value shows today's state crossed out next to the new state. Call stacks show a change the same way, with + rows for new code and - rows for code the change removes. See Diagram diffs .
The agent writes the plan in phases, each small enough to be one commit. When a phase is done, the spec shows a card for its commit with the files to review, most important first. Click a file to open its diff. Every link in the phase then points at that commit, so it keeps showing the code from that commit after the file changes.
Highlight text on the page and press Comment to leave a note beside it. In a diff, file excerpt, or the Diff panel, hover a line and press the + in the gutter, or drag it across several lines, to comment under those lines. Comments save in your browser (localStorage, per page) and survive reloads. Copy comments in the top right copies them all as a numbered Markdown list, each with its location and the quoted text or lines, ready to paste to an agent. ⌘/Ctrl-Enter saves a comment and Escape cancels it.
Bare npx @tanishqkancharla/diffmap path/to/file.md is the same as serve .
--port — pin a listen port (default: a free port)
--root — workspace root for file excerpts (default the directory you ran the command from)
Close server in the top right stops the server. Hosted gist and GitHub viewers have no local server, so they omit this control.
The server also stops after 24 hours without a page or source request. Loading or refreshing the page resets the timer; background health checks and Vite connections do not keep it alive.
List every running viewer, including viewers using custom ports:
Update a global install to the latest @tanishqkancharla/diffmap on npm. diffmap --update does the same thing:
If you are already on the latest version, it says so and exits. Otherwise it runs the global install for the package manager that installed diffmap ( npm install --global , pnpm add --global , or bun add --global ) and prints the old and new versions. Under npx , or when it cannot tell how diffmap was installed, it prints the command to run instead of installing anything.
Request the page with Accept: text/markdown to read the current source file instead of the rendered HTML. Use the URL printed by serve :
Share a spec with a link (experimental)
Share an unlisted gist and print a diffmap.dev link (requires gh logged in). Does not start a local server:
Hosted viewer: https://diffmap.dev/g/ (optional / ; #heading is the table of contents). The page fetches the gist in the browser from api.github.com . Gists are unlisted, not private.
A spec committed to a GitHub pull request also opens at https://diffmap.dev/ / /pull/ /specs/ .md .
parseViewerDocument turns markdown into the page document with md4x . startServer listens. The generate-diffmap skill owns document shape; the viewer does not.
Fences keep whitespace. Use them for mermaid, call stacks, and diffs.
In a code fence, {2,4-6} after the language highlights those lines. Comment lines at the bottom of the fence add notes that show on hover or keyboard focus:
[!note L3] or [!note L3-L5] notes a line range. Any other target is a symbol, and the note covers every whole-word occurrence in the fence.
Start note lines with // , # , or -- . The viewer removes them, so line numbers count only the code above. Backticks in a note render as code.
A symbol that does not appear, overlapping line notes, or a line number outside the fence is a parse error. A note line above other code stays code.
Add [Title] after the language to show a title above the code, as in ```ts [src/request.ts] {2-3} . Call stacks and mermaid fences take a title the same way, as in ```mermaid diff [Request flow] , or ::callstack{title="Request flow"} and ::mermaid{title="Request flow"} in MDC. A services fence uses its start caption instead.
Call stacks take the same highlights and notes, counting rows from the first. Write their notes with # . A symbol note matches the row text you see, not hidden references. Inside a linked row, symbol notes show on hover only; the row itself keeps keyboard focus.
Run npx @tanishqkancharla/diffmap fixtures/code-notes.md for an example.
md4x Comark components map to the same views:
::details folds its content under the summary label until the reader opens it. .md and .mdx are both markdown. Curly braces in prose are plain text.
Show screenshots and recordings with Markdown image syntax. Paths are relative to the spec file.
A .mp4 , .webm , .mov , .m4v , or .ogv file renders as a video player; anything else is an image. On its own line, it shows centered in a card, with its alt text as the title row. A title, as in ![alt](path "title") , shows on hover.
Group related images and videos in a gallery, with the layout after :::gallery :
side-by-side puts every item in one row, to compare before and after or one page at several widths.
grid wraps items into rows, to scan states or variants.
carousel shows one item at a time with Previous and Next (← and →), to step through a flow. Add a title after the layout, as in :::gallery carousel [Saving a record] ; it stays in the title row while the current item's label changes below it.
Each item's alt text is its visible label. A gallery holds only images and videos, and ::gallery{layout="grid"} works too. The syntax matches galleries in Amp threads.
serve loads media from beside the spec, and a spec on a GitHub pull request loads it from the same commit. share fails when a spec uses local media, because a gist holds only text files; link media by https URL to share it.
Run npx @tanishqkancharla/diffmap fixtures/media.md for an example.
Append a reference to a call stack line to link it. Paths are relative to --root .
[[path/to/file.ts#symbolName]] links a TypeScript or JavaScript declaration, including qualified names such as [[src/store.ts#Store.save]] . Ambiguous names show the qualified names you can use instead.
[[path/to/file]] links a whole file and [[path/to/file#L12-L30]] a line range. These work with any language.
[[ :path/to/file#L12-L30]] or [[ :path/to/file]] links a change in a commit. is a 7–40 character lowercase commit SHA, or a range .. .
A reference without a commit opens the Diff panel on uncommitted changes (working tree against HEAD), focused on that file or range. If the file has no uncommitted changes, the panel shows the current file.
A commit reference opens the Diff panel on every file changed in that commit or range, with a sticky header per file, scrolled to the linked file and lines. Line numbers are the file's lines after the commit. The file must be changed in that commit and the range must fit the new file; serve and share run git and fail at startup otherwise. Deleted lines cannot be referenced, and a commit cannot be combined with #symbol .
Multiple references on one stack line are allowed. The references are hidden in the rendered stack, and linked rows support mouse clicks and keyboard activation.
A changes fence shows a commit's files as a card. Each row shows the file name and +N −M. Review opens the Diff panel on all files; a row scrolls to that file without expanding its unchanged lines. An empty body (or working ) means uncommitted changes.
Lines after the rev list the files to review, in order. The card shows those first and folds the rest under a dimmed N other files row that expands and collapses. Review opens the Diff panel in the same order. serve and share fail if a listed file is not changed in that commit. With no list, the card shows every file.
References open in one shared panel beside the walkthrough. Selecting a stack line or diagram element highlights it and scrolls the panel to the linked code range. When a target has several references, buttons above the source viewer select among them. On narrow windows the source panel sits below the walkthrough. Documents without references keep the single-panel layout.
Malformed references produce a parse error.
On a GitHub-hosted spec, commit diffs come from the GitHub API. It returns patch hunks only, so only lines near changes are reachable, and the Diff button opens the pull request's full diff.
A shared gist is a snapshot taken when you run diffmap share . It saves every referenced commit and every changes card, including uncommitted ones, to diffmap-changes.json . It saves the current contents of every file that a file excerpt or a reference without a commit reads to diffmap-files.json . In the gist, those references open the saved file; symbols resolve to their first matching line, and Cmd-click definitions only work in a local viewer. Commit your work and point references at the commit before sharing, so the gist shows the diff instead of a bare file.
Cmd-click (or Ctrl-click) a TypeScript or JavaScript symbol in the source panel to open its definition. Use Back to retrace navigation and return to the reference. Resolution uses the workspace's TypeScript configuration and current files.
Run npx @tanishqkancharla/diffmap fixtures/annotations.md for an example with commit references, multiple files, and unchanged context.
A services fence shows services, their state, and the events they send each other, then replays those events step by step. Readers press Play , step with the arrow buttons or ← and →, or click the progress bar to jump to a step.
service "label" declares a service. Indent a service line under another to nest it. Names are unique within the diagram.
state = declares a value and its initial state. Indent it under its service.
start "caption" at column 0, before the first step, titles the whole diagram, such as start "Alice logs in" . It stays in the title row while the reader steps. A > line under it gives an overview of the whole process, shown under the title until the first step. A services fence takes no [Title] ; the start caption is its title.
step "caption" starts a step at column 0. The caption is required: a sentence that says what happens, shown under the title row above the controls. Indented lines under it are From -> To: label events and Service.key = value updates. A step's events travel one after another, in the order written, and the updates land when the last one arrives.
A > line adds text to the line above it. Indent it further than that line; consecutive > lines join. Under a service or state, it is a description: the name gets a dotted underline and the text shows in a tooltip on hover or focus. Under start or a step, it explains the caption and shows under it. Under an event or update, it is a note for that step. Notes appear in a column beside the diagram once the step's events land, each joined by a line to its event label or state row. Under a service name on its own line in a step, it is a note on that service for the step, joined by a line to the service box.

Under start or a step, it explains the caption and shows under it.
Under an event or update, it is a note for that step. Notes appear in a column beside the diagram once the step's events land, each joined by a line to its event label or state row.
Under a service name on its own line in a step, it is a note on that service for the step, joined by a line to the service box.
Append [[reference]] to a service line or an event to link it to source.
Services must be declared before the first step, and updates may only change declared state. ELK lays the services out left to right, or top to bottom when that fits the column better, and routes one connection between each pair of services that talk. A request and its reply share that connection. Indentation is significant, so services has no MDC form. See the runnable examples .
Add diff after mermaid or services to show a change in one diagram. Start every line with - for Today only, + for Proposed only, or a space for both, as in a call stack diff. Indentation starts after that column.
diffmap draws every line once, so both versions share one layout. Nodes, edges, sequence participants, and messages that only Today has are red and dashed; those only Proposed has are green. A node whose label differs between the versions is amber and shows its Proposed label. Each version must also be a valid diagram on its own. To relabel a node, declare it on its own line ( - B[Old] , + B[New] ) so its edges are not drawn twice. In a diff, %% ref edge: counts edges as drawn: within each run of changed lines, + lines come before - lines.
In a services diff , lines inside a - or + service or step take its sign. Today replays the unmarked and - lines and Proposed the unmarked and + lines, so each state row shows Today's value struck through beside Proposed's when they differ. A - and a + declaration of the same state key give each version its own starting value. Added and removed steps color their segment of the progress bar, and their caption starts with Added or Removed . See the runnable examples .
Inside a Mermaid fence, add %% ref node: [[reference]] to link a node or participant, or %% ref edge: [[reference]] to link an edge or sequence message. Edge indices start at zero in declaration order. The same file, symbol, and commit references work here. Keep one directive per target; append multiple references to that directive when needed.
Click a linked shape, edge line, or edge label, or focus it with Tab and press Enter or Space. Directives are Mermaid comments, so they remain hidden and do not change the diagram when rendered by other Mermaid tools. Missing diagram targets display an error. See the runnable example .
Write any reference in a paragraph, list item, or table cell, such as See [[src/store.ts#Store.save]] for the write path. or Close server landed in [[dae6b98:src/viewer/CloseServerButton.tsx]]. It renders as clickable inline code labeled with the file name and fragment ( store.ts#Store.save ) and opens the same source panel. References inside code spans and link text stay literal, so `[[path]]` shows the syntax itself.
Found a bug, hit a confusing error, or want a feature? Open an issue with what you did, what you expected, what happened, and your diffmap version ( diffmap --version ). Agents using the generate-diffmap skill do the same through gh issue create .
